# Intake brief — Remove dead local_max_concurrent_queries config; session_slot_pool_size is the single source of truth (LP-0MSG9PA95008GKLY)

## Problem statement

`local_max_concurrent_queries` was a legacy config key (introduced Jul 4, 2026) that shadowed the real concurrency limit. Both `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` and `provider._get_local_concurrency_info()` fell back to it, while the effective limit was always `session_slot_pool_size`. An operator reading `proxy/config.yaml` saw `local_max_concurrent_queries: 1` that was never applied (effective limit was 3), which is misleading and risks silent override if set.

## Users

- **Operator** — needs a single, unambiguous knob for local concurrency; not two keys where one silently wins.
- **On-call / reviewer** — needs config comments and docs to match the code so incident triage is not misled.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want exactly one config key (`session_slot_pool_size`) to control local concurrency, so I cannot be misled by a dead/misleading setting.
- As an operator, I want any legacy override to either be removed or to warn loudly, so a stale value cannot silently change behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No active config file (`proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`) contains `local_max_concurrent_queries` (verified by `rg` on checkout; remaining hits are docs/CHANGELOG/test comments referencing the removal — LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE).
2. `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` reads only `session_slot_pool_size` (no legacy fallback) and defaults safely; `provider._get_local_concurrency_info()` and `proxy/server.py` startup validation behave the same (FATAL if missing/invalid — per LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE).
3. Config comment at `server.session_slot_pool_size` states it is the single source of truth for local concurrency / `--parallel` (no ambiguous "preserved for explicit override" wording).
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (docs/llama-router.md already notes the removal).
5. Full project test suite passes with the new state; concurrency behaviour unchanged (limit = `session_slot_pool_size` = 3 in base config, 2 in cheap, 3 in fast).

## Constraints

- No behavioural change in normal operation (concurrency stays at `session_slot_pool_size`).
- Do not edit agent-infrastructure under `.pi/` per repo boundary rules — that fixture cleanup was tracked separately (LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W).
- Small scope, chore-class change; no new runtime semantics.

## Existing state

This item was filed Aug 5, 2026 during the busy-time analysis (LP-0MSG97N2F0090TO9). It has since been **superseded**:

- LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE (shipped v0.1.16, commits `7d9a24f` + `ccef0b6`) removed `local_max_concurrent_queries` from all three config files, from `router.py`/`provider.py`/`lifecycle.py`, added unconditional FATAL startup validation when `session_slot_pool_size` is missing/invalid, and updated lease/WebUI enrichment. Tests were migrated to assert the new behaviour. This work is on `origin/dev` and `HEAD`.
- LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W removed the remaining legacy line from the `proxy-usage-analysis` skill test fixture (`.pi/skills/.../fixtures.py`) — the `.pi/` edit the earlier item intentionally left out per boundary rules.
- Current `rg` on `HEAD` shows zero hits in `proxy/config*.yaml` or live code (remaining hits are intentional removal notes in comments/docs/tests/CHANGELOG).

So the work described here is already delivered; this item is a duplicate.

## Desired change

No code change. Close this item as a duplicate of LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE (with LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W as the `.pi/` follow-up). If the team prefers to keep a trace, keep the title and link the duplicate relation; do not re-implement.

Alternatives considered and rejected:
- Keep the legacy key with a deprecation warning — rejected in LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE in favour of full removal + FATAL validation (simpler, no silent override).

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Previously held `local_max_concurrent_queries: 1`; now only `session_slot_pool_size: 3` — verified no active key.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml` — Same; now `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — Same; now `session_slot_pool_size: 2`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` now reads only `session_slot_pool_size` (lines ~130-145).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_get_local_concurrency_info()` likewise (lines ~2270-2290).
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — Startup validation raises `ValueError` when `session_slot_pool_size` missing/invalid.
- `docs/llama-router.md` — Documents that legacy fallback was removed in favour of `session_slot_pool_size`.
- `proxy/tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py` — FATAL-validation tests (including missing-key case).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py` — Asserts helper reads only `session_slot_pool_size`.

## Related work

Potentially related docs:
- `proxy/config.yaml` (lines ~611, 698, 705) — `session_slot_pool_size` as pool/`--parallel` source.
- `proxy/README.md` (slot-schedule section) — time-based `session_slot_pool_size` semantics.
- `docs/llama-router.md` (lines ~273, 303) — documents removal of legacy fallback.
- `docs/systemd/llama-server.service` — notes alignment of `--parallel` with `session_slot_pool_size`.

Potentially related work items:
- LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE — **Remove local_max_concurrent_queries legacy key + add lease label to WebUI slot status** — `completed`/`done`, shipped v0.1.16 — **this item is a duplicate of LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE**.
- LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W — **Remove local_max_concurrent_queries from proxy-usage-analysis skill test fixture** — `completed`/`in_review`, follow-up for the `.pi/` fixture the earlier fix intentionally left.
- LP-0MSG97N2F0090TO9 — **Add local model busy-time report** — `completed`/`done` — discovery context for this cleanup.
- LP-0MRIKWYHM008LVLP — **Fix _get_local_concurrency_info to use session_slot_pool_size instead of local_max_concurrent_queries** — `completed`.
- LP-0MSCABA5K0010LW2 — Config-consistency validation (referenced in original ACs; not directly searched, listed in original description).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Team accepts closing as duplicate rather than re-doing the removal — if not, the alternative is a no-op verification pass.
- **Risk — Stale references:** Future contributors may reintroduce the key via copy-paste sample configs; mitigated by FATAL validation and `rg` in review.
- **Risk — Missed fixture:** Only remaining fixture hit was in `.pi/` and was cleaned by LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W; no further fixture clean-up needed here.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not expand to unrelated slot/config refactors; file new items for extra opportunities (e.g., docs polish).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is this item still needed given LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE shipped the removal?" — Answer (Map, agent): No code change needed; verify via `rg` + `wl show` that the removal is on `HEAD`/`origin/dev` and propose closing as duplicate of LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE. Source: `rg -n local_max_concurrent_queries` on HEAD (zero active config/code hits), `wl show LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE --json` (stage `done`, shipped v0.1.16), `wl show LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W` (fixture follow-up).
- Q: "Should `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` be edited in this item?" — Answer (Map, agent): No — `.pi/` is agent infrastructure per repo boundary rules; that edit was intentionally deferred and is tracked as LP-0MTD4C1HN005I48W. Source: repo boundary guidance in AGENTS.md; LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE comment by `pi`.
- Q: "What verification replaces an interview for this duplicate?" — Answer (Map, agent): Repo search + worklog trace replaces interview; no clarifying questions were posed to the producer because the seed context and worklog history fully define the outcome. Source: `wl search` + `rg` evidence above.

*No open questions.*

# Intake Brief — Add compaction fallback model chain (OpenRouter → Muse → local Qwen3)

**Work Item:** LP-0MTSDDD4E004DNF0
**Parent:** LP-0MTPK77WG009A4VH — Investigate Muse compaction hang via Responses API translation layer
**Type:** feature
**Priority:** medium

**Headline:** Add a three-tier cascading fallback chain for proxy-side session compaction summarization (OpenRouter free → Muse on OpenCode → local Qwen3) so compaction continues reliably even when the local model is unavailable.

## Problem Statement

The proxy-side session compaction summarizer currently supports only a single local model (Qwen3 via llama-server). When the local model is unavailable or under heavy GPU contention, compaction silently falls through to non-compactable sessions. A cascading fallback chain — OpenRouter free tier → Muse on OpenCode → local Qwen3 — would significantly improve compaction reliability.

## Users

- **Proxy operators** — need compaction to work reliably regardless of local GPU availability, without additional infrastructure
- **Pi users** — benefit from compacted sessions maintaining fast response times across long conversations

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Config defines a three-tier fallback chain:** The proxy config includes a `summarizer_model` section with a cascading fallback chain: OpenRouter (`google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`) → Muse on OpenCode (`muse-spark-1.2-contributor`) → local Qwen3.
2. **AC2 — OpenRouter primary summarizer works:** When configured with a valid `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env var, the summarizer calls OpenRouter's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` as the model, using the same summarizer prompt and response parsing as the local summarizer.
3. **AC3 — Cascading fallback on failure:** If the OpenRouter call fails (HTTP error, timeout, or empty response), the summarizer transparently retries with Muse via the existing OpenCode remote provider configuration. If Muse also fails, it falls back to the local Qwen3 summarizer.
4. **AC4 — Fail-open behavior preserved:** The summarizer returns empty string on any failure at any tier (never blocks dispatch). Each fallback transition is logged at WARNING level with the failure reason.
5. **AC5 — Existing local-only behavior unchanged when config omits remote tiers:** If `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is not set or the config does not specify a remote summarizer, the system falls back directly to local Qwen3 (the current behavior).

## Constraints

- **No new infrastructure dependencies** — must use existing proxy remote-call infrastructure (httpx for OpenRouter, existing OpenCode provider config for Muse).
- **Must not break existing compaction** — all existing local-only summarizer behavior must be preserved as the final fallback.
- **Timeout must be bounded** — each tier has a configurable timeout (default 30s) so compaction never stalls.
- **Config change is additive** — existing `summarizer_model: {type: local, llama_model: Qwen3}` config should continue to work (local-only path).

## Existing State

- **Current summarizer:** Single local model — `proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` builds a `Summarizer` callable backed by `llama-server` on port 8080, using `summarizer_model.llama_model` from config.
- **Config structure:** `server.summarizer_model` in `config.yaml` — currently only supports `{type: local, llama_model: Qwen3}`.
- **Compaction wiring:** `router_helpers.py:_evaluate_session_compaction` receives the summarizer callable and passes it to `decide_session_compaction`.
- **OpenRouter in proxy:** No OpenRouter provider currently configured in `config.yaml`. OpenRouter model IDs exist in `provider_resolver.py` mapping tables but are not used as remote providers.
- **OpenCode Muse:** Configured in `plan`, `author`, `code` model providers as `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `opencode-go` provider with `api: openai-responses`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Add `summarizer_model` with remote + local fallback entries
- `proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — Extend `build_local_summarizer` (or create `build_fallback_summarizer`) to support multi-tier dispatch
- `proxy/provider.py` — Update `compaction_config()` to parse the new fallback chain structure
- `proxy/router_helpers.py` — Update call site to use the new fallback summarizer builder

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: OpenRouter rate limits** — The free model tier on OpenRouter may have aggressive rate limits that cause compaction timeouts. Mitigation: bounded timeouts + automatic fallback to next tier.
- **Risk: OpenRouter API key availability** — Requires `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env var to be set. If absent, system must gracefully skip OpenRouter tier and fall through to local. This is handled by the "existing local-only behavior unchanged" constraint.
- **Risk: Compaction latency increase** — Three-tier fallback could increase worst-case compaction latency. Mitigation: each tier has a bounded timeout (default 30s); overall timeout cap.
- **Scope creep: full multi-model routing** — This change is scoped to compaction summarization only. Do not expand to other model routing paths (plan/author/code) without separate work items.
- **Assumption: OpenRouter /v1/chat/completions endpoint format** — OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible, so the same request/response format as the local llama-server should work.
- **Assumption: Muse via OpenCode supports the summarizer prompt format** — Muse is already used as a fallback in plan/author/code providers, so it should work.

## Related Work

- **LP-0MTPK77WG009A4VH** — Investigate Muse compaction hang via Responses API translation layer (parent)
- **LP-0MTPMJG1P0038D32** — Implement proxy-side summarizer backed by local Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MTPMJGC3007YG0S** — Wire the summarizer + routing estimator into _evaluate_session_compaction (in review)
- **LP-0MTPMEQ5V005CMZ7** — Evaluate OpenRouter free models for proxy-side summarization (evaluation; this item supersedes with implementation)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What is the fallback chain?" — Answer (user): "google/gemma-4-31b-it:free via OpenRouter → muse on opencode → local Qwen3". Source: user request.
- Q: "Should this replace the existing local summarizer or be additive?" — Answer (inferred from spec): Additive — the existing local Qwen3 is the final fallback tier. Source: user said "falling back to muse on opencode, falling back to the local Qwen model."
